{{Short description|American mathematician (1941–2020)}}[[File:Peter Antonelli, Edmonton, Alberta, Canada (August, 2010).jpg|thumb|Photo of Peter L. Antonelli (American mathematician) in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada (August. 2010)]]'''Peter Louis Antonelli''' (March 5, 1941 – February 15, 2020) was an American mathematician known for his work on [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|mathematical biology]], [[Finsler geometry]], and their connections.

== Overview ==
Antonelli was born on March 5, 1941, in [[Syracuse, New York]], and became a student at [[Syracuse University]], graduating in 1963.<ref name="pla60">{{cite book
 | last1 = Anastasiei | first1 = M.
 | last2 = Antonelli | first2 = P. L.
 | editor-first1 = M
 | editor-first2 = P. L
 | editor-last1 = Anastasiei
 | editor-last2 = Antonelli
 | doi = 10.1007/978-94-017-0405-2
 | publisher = Springer Netherlands
 | title = Finsler and Lagrange Geometries: Proceedings of a Conference held on August 26–31, Iaşi, Romania
 | year = 2003| isbn = 978-90-481-6325-0
 }} See especially Radi Miron and Mihai Anastasiei, "Professor Dr. Peter Louis Antonelli at Sixty", pp. xi–xiii.</ref> He completed a PhD at Syracuse University, with the 1966 dissertation ''Structure Theory for Montgomery-Samelson Fiberings Between Manifolds'' supervised by Erik Hemmingsen.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alumni|url=https://thecollege.syr.edu/mathematics/graduate-studies/alumni/|access-date=2022-01-16|website=College of Arts & Sciences at Syracuse University|language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=367}}</ref>

After a short period as assistant professor at the [[University of Tennessee]], Knoxville from 1967 to 1968, and an NSF post-doctoral fellowship at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], from 1968 to 1970, he took a faculty position at the [[University of Alberta]], Canada, where he stayed for the remainder of his career.<ref name="pla60" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Retired Faculty {{!}} Mathematical and Statistical Sciences|url=https://www.ualberta.ca/mathematical-and-statistical-sciences/people/retired-faculty.html|access-date=2022-01-14|website=www.ualberta.ca}}</ref> In 2006, he moved to Brazil with his wife and colleague S.F. Rutz, where he was a visiting professor at [[Federal University of Pernambuco]], Recife.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Peter Louis Antonelli|url=https://www.escavador.com/sobre/400617/peter-louis-antonelli|access-date=2022-01-16|website=Escavador|language=pt-br}}</ref>

He died in 2020.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Gielis | first1 = Johan
 | last2 = Goemans | first2 = Wendy
 | doi = 10.2991/gaf.k.200131.001
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Growth and Form
 | page = 44
 | title = Editorial
 | volume = 1
 | year = 2020| s2cid = 243398589
 | doi-access = free
 }}</ref>
== Contributions to mathematics ==
In his early years, Peter L. Antonelli's interests were focused on physics, especially [[general relativity]]. As a Ph.D. student, he studied mathematical objects such as special groups of [[diffeomorphism]]s and [[Exotic sphere|exotic spheres]]. After 1970, his interests shifted towards applied mathematics, especially applications of [[differential geometry]] to [[developmental biology]], [[ecology]], and [[genetics]]. As a visiting professor in the biology department at the [[University of Sussex]] in the early 1970s,  he pursued interests that had developed from his work in the early 1960s as a United States Public Health Service Fellow in mathematical biology at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name=pla60/>

During the course of his career, Peter L. Antonelli published over 120 research papers in a variety of domains including non-linear mechanics, [[Hamiltonian system|Hamiltonian systems]], [[diffusion theory]], [[stochastic calculus]] and [[stochastic geometry]], [[geometric probability]], differential [[game theory]], [[bifurcation theory]], geometry of paths, and  [[Riemannian geometry|Riemannian]], [[Finsler manifold|Finslerian]] and Lagrangian geometries. The geometry of certain non-Riemannian metrics now bear his name.<ref name=pla60/> Along with his extensive work on the mathematical ecology of the [[Great Barrier Reef]],<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sapp |first=Jan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1KKqMm1kyxIC&dq=coral+reefs+peter+antonelli&pg=PA184 |title=What is Natural?: Coral Reef Crisis |date=2003 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-516178-6 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bradbury |first=R. H. |date=1991 |title=UNDERSTANDING "ACANTHÁSTER" |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43461274 |journal=Coenoses |volume=6 |issue=3 |pages=121–126 |jstor=43461274 |issn=0393-9154}}</ref> he also showed that all living plants and animals are likely derived from two primitive species of bacteria, through the process of [[endosymbiosis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Researchers Show Evolutionary Theory Adds Up |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2004/01/040113075946.htm |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=ScienceDaily |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Researchers show evolutionary theory adds up |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/790305 |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=EurekAlert! |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first=Bob |last=Holmes |date=24 January 2004  |title=Early life wouldn't stand a chance in a commune |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg18124311-400-early-life-wouldnt-stand-a-chance-in-a-commune/ |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Whitfield |first=John |date=2004-02-19 |title=  Born in a watery commune|url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?p=HRCA&sw=w&issn=00280836&v=2.1&it=r&id=GALE%7CA186371433&sid=googleScholar&linkaccess=abs |journal=Nature |language=English |volume=427 |issue=6976 |pages=674–677|doi=10.1038/427674a |pmid=14973452 |bibcode=2004Natur.427..674W |s2cid=28739859 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1987, Antonelli was awarded a McCalla Professorship at the University of Alberta for research excellence. In 2001, he was awarded the degree of Honorary Professor from [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University]] in Romania. Papers from a conference held there in honor of his 60th birthday were later published as a [[festschrift]].<ref name=pla60/>
